assumptions: Node is a concrete sociolinguistic/pragmatic work-unit, method, or decision area, not a topic label.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
The user's multilingual context (Punjabi/Hindi/English) is treated as a running exemplar, not the only scope.
Scope spans variation, multilingualism, pragmatics, and discourse as a single coherent subdomain of linguistics.
exclusions: Formal phonology, morphology, and syntax except where they condition a sociolinguistic variable.
First/second-language acquisition pedagogy and clinical linguistics.
Language documentation of undescribed languages and historical reconstruction beyond change-in-progress.
Computational NLP model building (separate AI/computing subdomains).

competency_questions.question: For a sociolinguistic/pragmatic question, what variety, community, and sampling frame should the search target?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_VARIETY_FRAME present and first in priority_order

competency_questions.question: How is a vague construct (prestige, politeness, register) operationalized into searchable indicators?
How is variation (variable rules, style, register) located and appraised for a variety?
How is regional dialect variation and language change in progress evidenced and dated?
How are prestige and language attitudes appraised without confusing evaluation with description?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRESTIGE_ATTITUDE_EVAL present with the prestige-vs-description axis

competency_questions.question: How is a multilingual repertoire profiled and code-switching classified for a community like Punjabi/Hindi/English?
How are contact outcomes, diglossia, and maintenance/shift distinguished and sourced?
How are speech acts, implicatures, and deixis identified to recover speaker meaning in context?
How is politeness/face-work and presupposition appraised across cultures?
How is discourse cohesion/coherence and conversational structure analyzed?
How is identity and social meaning shown to be co-constructed and indexed in discourse?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCOURSE_IDENTITY present and built on CONVERSATION_ANALYSIS

competency_questions.question: How are sources appraised and findings synthesized with honest transfer limits to the target community?

glossary.definition: a feature with two or more variants whose use co-varies with social/linguistic factors
alternation between languages/varieties within a single interaction or utterance
an item from a donor language integrated into a recipient language's system
a stable allocation of High and Low varieties to distinct domains of use
what a speaker does in saying something (asserting, requesting, promising)
meaning conveyed beyond what is literally said, inferable and often cancellable
reference whose interpretation depends on the utterance context (person/place/time/discourse)
the public self-image a participant claims and others may threaten or support
background content a sentence takes for granted, surviving negation/questioning
the way a linguistic form points to social meaning or context
the degree to which a finding from one community holds for the target community

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from standard sociolinguistics and pragmatics literature (e.g., Wardhaugh & Fuller, An Introduction to Sociolinguistics; Yule, The Study of Language; Labov; Holmes; Myers-Scotton; Levinson; Brown & Levinson; Sacks/Schegloff CA) and field practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix the language variety, speech community, and sampling frame whose sociolinguistic/pragmatic knowledge is being searched, so retrieval targets the right population.

excluded: language documentation of an undescribed language

contradictors: essentialist who treats a language as monolithic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the question shifts to a different variety or community

pros.claim: prevents conflating distinct varieties or communities in retrieval
pros.example: searching 'Punjabi' without fixing Majhi vs Pothohari vs diaspora variety

cons.claim: an over-broad frame imports irrelevant or contradictory findings
cons.example: treating all 'Hindi-Urdu' work as one undifferentiated source

failure_modes: community boundary drawn by language name only
acceptance_tests: variety, community, and sampling frame are explicitly stated
exclusions from the frame are listed

nodes.definition: Turn a vague sociolinguistic/pragmatic notion (prestige, politeness, register) into a measurable variable with explicit indicators before searching for evidence about it.
contradictors: theorist who resists operational reduction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the construct's accepted operationalization changes

pros.claim: makes 'prestige' or 'politeness' searchable as concrete indicators
pros.example: operationalizing prestige via overt-vs-covert evaluation tasks

cons.claim: a bad operationalization invalidates every downstream finding
cons.example: measuring politeness only by please/thank-you tokens

acceptance_tests: each construct has at least one observable indicator
indicator validity is argued against the construct

nodes.definition: Locate and appraise the canonical sociolinguistic variable studies (Labov-style) that quantify how a linguistic variable co-varies with social factors.
contradictors: formalist who denies orderly heterogeneity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a replication revises the factor weights

pros.claim: grounds variation claims in quantified social conditioning
pros.example: (ng) variable stratified by class and style in NYC

cons.claim: factor weights are corpus-specific and may not transfer
cons.example: applying Detroit constraints to a Punjabi-English community

revisit_triggers: new variable rule study supersedes prior

nodes.definition: Find and evaluate accounts of intra-speaker style-shifting and register variation (attention-to-speech, audience design, indexicality).
contradictors: one who treats style as random noise

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a richer model of stylistic agency is adopted

pros.claim: explains why one speaker varies across situations
pros.example: a speaker shifting to standard forms in a job interview

cons.claim: competing models (attention vs audience vs stance) are hard to adjudicate
cons.example: forcing audience-design onto a stance phenomenon

nodes.definition: Retrieve and assess dialectological/geolinguistic evidence (isoglosses, dialect continua, atlases) delimiting regional varieties.
contradictors: one who imposes discrete dialect borders

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when newer geolinguistic survey data appears

pros.claim: separates regional from social variation in the search
pros.example: Punjabi dialect continuum from Lahore to Delhi

cons.claim: atlas data ages quickly and may misrepresent current speech
cons.example: relying on a mid-20th-century atlas for current usage

nodes.definition: Distinguish and source apparent-time vs real-time evidence of ongoing language change, including prestige-driven shifts.
contradictors: one who confounds age-grading with change

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when real-time data revises an apparent-time inference

pros.claim: prevents mistaking age-grading for genuine change
pros.example: reading teenage slang as community-wide change

cons.claim: apparent-time can mislead when age-grading is present
cons.example: inferring change from a single age-stratified snapshot

nodes.definition: Source and appraise evidence on overt/covert prestige and language attitudes (matched-guise, evaluation studies) that drive evaluation of varieties.
contradictors: prescriptivist equating prestige with correctness

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a methodologically stronger attitude study appears

pros.claim: explains why low-prestige forms persist via covert prestige
pros.example: vernacular forms signaling local loyalty

cons.claim: attitude measures are method-sensitive and ideology-laden
cons.example: matched-guise confounding voice quality with variety

failure_modes: attitude method artifact treated as fact
revisit_triggers: new attitude study reverses prior finding

nodes.definition: Characterize a speaker's or community's multilingual repertoire and dominance configuration before sourcing claims about their multilingual behavior.
contradictors: monolingual-norm theorist

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the repertoire or dominance configuration changes

pros.claim: prevents treating a multilingual speaker as two monolinguals
pros.example: a Punjabi/Hindi/English speaker with domain-split usage

cons.claim: static dominance labels miss fluid, contextual use
cons.example: labeling a speaker 'English-dominant' ignoring home Punjabi

nodes.definition: Locate and appraise frameworks for code-switching/mixing (structural constraints, Matrix-Language, conversational functions) to classify observed switches.
contradictors: purist treating CS as deficient mixing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the structural or functional model of CS is revised

pros.claim: separates rule-governed switching from random mixing
pros.example: intra-sentential Punjabi-English switch obeying ML constraints

cons.claim: competing CS models disagree on the same data
cons.example: constraint-based vs functional accounts of one switch

nodes.definition: Source and evaluate evidence on contact outcomes (borrowing, interference, convergence, pidgin/creole genesis, shift) to explain contact-induced features.
contradictors: one who attributes all change to internal drift

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when feature-source attribution is challenged

pros.claim: attributes a feature to contact vs internal change defensibly
pros.example: retroflex spread across South Asian languages as areal

cons.claim: contact vs internal causation is often underdetermined
cons.example: crediting contact for a change with an internal pathway

nodes.definition: Identify and appraise diglossia/domain-allocation analyses (High/Low varieties, domains of use) governing which variety is used where.
contradictors: one who equates diglossia with mere bilingualism

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when domain allocation or H/L assignment changes

pros.claim: explains principled variety choice across domains
pros.example: formal Hindi in school vs Punjabi at home

cons.claim: diglossia is often leaky and overstated as rigid
cons.example: treating a fluid repertoire as strict H/L diglossia

nodes.definition: Source and appraise evidence on language maintenance, shift, endangerment, and the policy/ideology context that drives them.
contradictors: one who treats shift as natural and value-free

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when transmission or policy evidence updates vitality

pros.claim: frames whether a variety is being transmitted or lost
pros.example: reduced Punjabi transmission among diaspora youth

cons.claim: vitality scales compress complex situations
cons.example: a single EGIDS number hiding domain-by-domain variation

nodes.definition: Identify illocutionary force and felicity conditions of utterances (locution/illocution/perlocution, direct vs indirect acts) as the core pragmatic work unit.
contradictors: semanticist reducing meaning to truth conditions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when context or cultural norm changes the assigned force

pros.claim: separates what is said from what is done with words
pros.example: 'can you pass the salt' as a request, not a question

cons.claim: indirectness and culture make force assignment uncertain
cons.example: reading an indirect refusal as literal agreement

failure_modes: literal force mistaken for intended force
acceptance_tests: each utterance is assigned an illocutionary force with justification
direct vs indirect status is argued

nodes.definition: Derive and appraise conversational/conventional implicatures via Gricean maxims and neo-Gricean/relevance accounts to recover unstated meaning.
contradictors: one who collapses implicature into entailment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a competing implicature account better fits the data

pros.claim: recovers meaning the speaker implied but did not state
pros.example: 'some students passed' implicating not all

cons.claim: cancellability and competing frameworks complicate derivation
cons.example: treating a cancellable implicature as fixed entailment

nodes.definition: Resolve context-dependent reference: person/spatial/temporal/discourse deixis and anaphora, anchoring expressions to the utterance context.
contradictors: one who treats reference as context-free

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the deictic anchor or discourse center moves

pros.claim: prevents misreading 'here/now/you' without an anchor
pros.example: resolving 'meet me here tomorrow' to a fixed place/time

cons.claim: deictic shift and reported speech create ambiguity
cons.example: mis-anchoring deixis inside quoted speech

nodes.definition: Source and appraise politeness frameworks (face, positive/negative politeness, FTAs, im/politeness) to evaluate interpersonal management in talk.
contradictors: one who treats politeness as universal and acultural

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a culture-specific politeness norm overrides a universal model

pros.claim: explains strategy choice behind a request or refusal
pros.example: hedging a request to reduce a face threat

cons.claim: Brown-Levinson universals are contested cross-culturally
cons.example: forcing negative-politeness universals onto a culture

nodes.definition: Identify presupposition triggers and assess their projection/accommodation across logical operators and discourse contexts.
contradictors: one who treats presupposition as ordinary entailment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the projection or accommodation analysis is revised

pros.claim: separates background assumptions from asserted content
pros.example: 'stopped smoking' presupposing prior smoking

cons.claim: projection is theory-dependent and context-sensitive
cons.example: mispredicting projection under negation or modals

nodes.definition: Analyze how a text holds together via cohesive devices (reference, conjunction, lexical cohesion) and coherence relations.
contradictors: one who treats a text as a bag of sentences

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the coherence-relation framework is revised

pros.claim: explains why a text reads as connected or disjointed
pros.example: tracking reference chains across paragraphs

cons.claim: coherence relation inventories disagree
cons.example: forcing one RST taxonomy onto ambiguous relations

nodes.definition: Apply conversation-analytic methods (turn-taking, adjacency pairs, repair, sequence organization) to naturally occurring interaction.
contradictors: one who imposes pre-set categories on talk

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when finer transcription revises the sequential analysis

pros.claim: reveals interactional order from participants' own orientations
pros.example: repair sequences showing trouble in understanding

cons.claim: CA resists generalization and demands fine transcription
cons.example: over-generalizing one repair pattern to all talk

failure_modes: analyst categories imposed over participant orientations

nodes.definition: Source and appraise interactional accounts of how identity, stance, and social meaning are indexed and co-constructed in discourse.
contradictors: essentialist correlating form to fixed identity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the indexical or stance analysis is reframed

pros.claim: explains social meaning as emergent, not pre-given
pros.example: a feature indexing local toughness in interaction

cons.claim: indexical claims are hard to falsify
cons.example: reading any feature as identity work without evidence

nodes.definition: Evaluate the authority, method, recency, and grounding of each sociolinguistic/pragmatic source before admitting its claims into the synthesis.
contradictors: citation-counter ignoring method quality

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a source's authority or method is re-appraised

pros.claim: keeps weak or outdated claims out of the synthesis
pros.example: rejecting a small-sample attitude study as authoritative

cons.claim: authority heuristics can suppress valid minority findings
cons.example: dismissing a small community study purely on sample size

acceptance_tests: each admitted source has a method+recency appraisal
inadmissible sources are recorded with reasons
revisit_triggers: method critique of a source emerges

nodes.definition: Integrate appraised findings into an answer and judge how far each claim transfers to the target variety/community, flagging over-generalization.
contradictors: one who universalizes findings from one community

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new admitted source changes the synthesis or transfer judgment

pros.claim: produces a defensible answer with explicit transfer caveats
pros.example: noting that NYC (r) findings need not hold for Punjabi-English

cons.claim: forcing a synthesis hides genuine cross-community disagreement
cons.example: averaging contradictory attitude findings into a false consensus

acceptance_tests: every synthesized claim states its community of origin and transfer limit

edges.why_related: constructs are operationalized only after the variety/community is fixed
edges.example: operationalizing prestige before fixing the community

edges.why_related: variationist analysis needs operational variables
edges.example: running factor analysis on a vague notion

edges.why_related: style/register study needs operationalized stylistic dimensions
edges.example: claiming style-shift without an indicator

edges.why_related: dialect mapping needs a defined geographic/variety frame
edges.example: drawing isoglosses without a defined region

edges.why_related: change-in-progress is read off variable analyses across age
edges.example: claiming change from one snapshot
edges.resolution_rule: establish the variable before inferring change

edges.why_related: attitude work needs operationalized prestige
edges.example: scoring prestige with no indicator

edges.why_related: repertoire profiling needs the community fixed
edges.example: profiling 'bilinguals' with no community

edges.why_related: CS classification needs the repertoire and dominance known
edges.example: assigning a matrix language with no dominance data

edges.why_related: contact outcomes are read against the repertoire and contact history
edges.example: crediting contact with no repertoire data

edges.why_related: domain allocation needs the repertoire and domains known
edges.example: assigning H/L with no domain data

edges.why_related: maintenance/shift is judged against the repertoire and transmission
edges.example: scoring vitality with no transmission data

edges.why_related: speech-act work needs an operational notion of force
edges.example: labeling force with no felicity test

edges.why_related: implicature derivation builds on identified illocutionary acts
edges.example: deriving implicature before fixing the act

edges.why_related: reference resolution supports act interpretation
edges.example: reading a request with an unresolved 'you'

edges.why_related: face-work is analyzed over identified acts (e.g., FTAs)
edges.example: scoring face-threat with no act

edges.why_related: presupposition is assessed over the asserted act
edges.example: testing projection with no act

edges.why_related: discourse cohesion analysis needs operational devices
edges.example: claiming coherence with no relations

edges.why_related: interaction analysis builds on text-level cohesion concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: CA done with no cohesion base
edges.example: analyzing turns ignoring reference chains

edges.why_related: identity/indexicality work builds on sequential analysis
edges.example: claiming identity work with no sequence

edges.why_related: source appraisal is applied to claims about operationalized constructs
edges.example: appraising a source with no question

edges.why_related: only appraised sources feed synthesis
edges.example: building an answer from weak sources

edges.why_related: transfer judgment needs the target variety/community fixed
edges.example: claiming transfer with no target community

edges.why_related: variable factor weights shape how style-shift is interpreted
edges.example: style read off the same variable as inter-speaker
edges.resolution_rule: treat style as intra-speaker layer of the variable

edges.why_related: prestige and attitudes drive the direction of change
edges.example: crediting change to prestige with no mechanism
edges.resolution_rule: require an attitude->change pathway, not mere correlation

edges.why_related: synchronic switching and diachronic borrowing form a continuum
edges.example: treating a nonce switch as an established loan
edges.resolution_rule: use frequency/integration to place an item on the continuum

edges.why_related: domain allocation drives intergenerational transmission and shift
edges.risk_of_conflict: domain loss read as automatic shift
edges.example: predicting shift from one lost domain
edges.resolution_rule: require transmission evidence, not domain count alone

edges.why_related: face-work and identity indexing both build social meaning in interaction
edges.example: reading every politeness move as identity work
edges.resolution_rule: keep face strategy and identity claims distinct

edges.why_related: indirectness for politeness is implemented via implicature
edges.example: explaining indirectness twice
edges.resolution_rule: attribute indirectness to face motive plus implicature mechanism

edges.why_related: intra-speaker style vs inter-speaker variation compete to explain the same tokens
edges.risk_of_conflict: attributing one token to both layers
edges.example: crediting a shift to class and to style at once
edges.resolution_rule: decompose variance: inter-speaker first, residual to style

edges.why_related: synchronic code-switching vs diachronic borrowing compete to label an item
edges.risk_of_conflict: an item labeled both nonce-switch and loan
edges.example: calling an integrated loan a switch

edges.why_related: universalist face theory vs culture-specific act interpretation pull opposite ways
edges.risk_of_conflict: forcing a universal strategy onto a culture
edges.example: reading an indirect refusal via B&L universals only
edges.resolution_rule: let culture-specific act norms cap universal politeness models

edges.why_related: pressure to synthesize a general answer conflicts with corpus-specific factor weights
edges.risk_of_conflict: exporting one corpus's weights as universal
edges.example: applying NYC weights to a Punjabi-English community
edges.resolution_rule: cap synthesis at the demonstrated community; flag transfer as a hypothesis

edges.why_related: synthesizing a cross-cultural politeness claim conflicts with culture-specific evidence
edges.example: claiming a universal politeness rule
edges.resolution_rule: report culture-specific findings separately; no forced universal

edges.why_related: emergent-indexical identity vs fixed demographic correlation compete to explain a feature
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps social meaning from being reified
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading a variable as a fixed identity badge
edges.example: mapping a feature one-to-one onto a demographic
edges.resolution_rule: prefer interactional evidence; correlation is a prior, not the meaning

edges.why_related: a contradiction surfaced in synthesis triggers re-appraisal of sources
edges.example: re-appraising after every minor mismatch
edges.resolution_rule: revisit only on material contradiction; stop after two appraisal passes

edges.why_related: a transfer failure triggers re-scoping of the target variety/community
edges.example: re-scoping on any caveat
edges.resolution_rule: re-scope only when transfer is systematically blocked; stop after one re-scope

edges.why_related: real-time disconfirmation triggers revisiting the variable analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: loops on every new data point
edges.example: revisiting on each new token
edges.resolution_rule: revisit only when real-time data contradicts apparent-time; stop after revalidation

edges.why_related: areal contact features inform where dialect boundaries are drawn
edges.example: drawing isoglosses ignoring a Sprachbund
edges.resolution_rule: consider areal/contact features when interpreting isoglosses

edges.why_related: deictic anchoring supports turn-by-turn reference tracking in talk
edges.example: anchoring 'here' ignoring the turn structure
edges.resolution_rule: resolve deixis within the sequential context

conflict_axes.trigger: the same tokens are attributable to social-group variation or to individual style-shift
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: inter-speaker conditioning is fixed before stylistic residual is interpreted
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the two layers cannot be separated in the data
conflict_axes.example: a class-stratified token that is also a style marker

conflict_axes.trigger: an item could be a nonce code-switch or an established borrowing
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: integration plus community-wide frequency dominates toward borrowing; otherwise switch
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if integration and frequency evidence conflict
conflict_axes.example: an English noun used by Punjabi monolinguals too

conflict_axes.trigger: universal pragmatic models clash with culture-specific interpretation
resolution_order: apply universal model only as a default
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: culture-specific evidence caps universal models when they conflict
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a universal model would mislabel a culturally normal act
conflict_axes.example: directness norms differing across South Asian vs Anglo contexts

conflict_axes.trigger: apparent-time inference may be age-grading rather than change
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: real-time evidence dominates apparent-time when available
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if only apparent-time data exists for a strong claim
conflict_axes.example: teenage forms that recede with age

conflict_axes.trigger: a general answer is wanted but findings are community-specific
resolution_order: state each finding's community of origin
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: community-specific evidence dominates; transfer to the target is a flagged hypothesis
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no target-community evidence exists yet a general claim is demanded
conflict_axes.example: exporting Detroit constraints to a diaspora Punjabi community

conflict_axes.trigger: a feature can be explained structurally or by its interactional function
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interactional evidence dominates when it is available and clear
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if structure and function give incompatible analyses
conflict_axes.example: a switch explained by ML grammar vs by a conversational move

conflict_axes.trigger: prestige/standard ideology pressures descriptions toward the standard variety
resolution_order: describe the vernacular on its own terms
record the ideology as data not norm
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: descriptive adequacy dominates; prestige is data about attitudes, not a norm
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a description is being skewed toward the standard
conflict_axes.example: treating a stigmatized form as an 'error' rather than a variant

conflict_axes.trigger: a meaning could be semantically encoded or pragmatically inferred
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: cancellable, context-dependent meaning is pragmatic; non-cancellable is semantic

edge_cases.trigger: a synthesis cites a node/source id that does not resolve
edge_cases.example: a transfer record references a dropped source id
edge_cases.detection_method: run reference-resolution check over all evidence_refs

edge_cases.trigger: an object omits a required schema field
a heuristic estimate is presented as observed
edge_cases.example: labeling a factor weight 'observed' with no dataset
edge_cases.detection_method: scan for observed/experimentally_validated labels with no data source

edge_cases.trigger: one node tries to cover switching and all contact outcomes
edge_cases.example: merging CS, borrowing, and creole genesis into one node
edge_cases.detection_method: check node scope against the grain rule

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk node lacks acceptance tests
edge_cases.example: a risk>=0.80 node with empty acceptance_tests
edge_cases.detection_method: flag high-risk nodes with empty acceptance_tests

edge_cases.trigger: a synthesis is hard-locked before appraisal and review pass
edge_cases.example: locking an answer before source appraisal completes

edge_cases.trigger: feedback revisit loops without a stop condition
edge_cases.example: re-appraising sources on every trivial mismatch
edge_cases.detection_method: check feedback edges for stop conditions

edge_cases.trigger: a tradeoff is encoded as a dependency
edge_cases.example: modeling inter-vs-intra tension as a prerequisite
edge_cases.detection_method: check that tradeoffs are conflict edges not dependencies

edge_cases.trigger: a dependent node is prioritized before its prerequisite
a finding rests on an outdated atlas/study
edge_cases.example: current usage inferred from a 1950s atlas
edge_cases.detection_method: check recency in the source appraisal

edge_cases.trigger: a community-specific finding is generalized to the target
edge_cases.example: applying one community's prestige finding to all
edge_cases.detection_method: check every synthesized claim for a transfer caveat

edge_cases.trigger: a template placeholder or illegal evidence label survives
edge_cases.example: an 'observed' label with no dataset or an unfilled template token surviving in a claim
edge_cases.detection_method: scan for placeholders and illegal labels
resolution: replace with domain value or heuristic

workflow.objective: fix the variety/community and operationalize the target constructs
acceptance_tests: variety, community, and sampling frame stated
workflow.do_first_because: no retrieval is valid until the population and constructs are fixed

workflow.objective: retrieve and appraise variation evidence (variable rules, style/register, dialect maps)

handoff_artifact.required_contents: variable analysis dossier;style/register appraisal;dialect boundary appraisal

workflow.do_first_because: variation is the empirical backbone for change, prestige, and transfer judgments

acceptance_tests: change status tagged apparent vs real time
workflow.do_first_because: age-grading and method artifacts must be screened before any change/prestige claim

workflow.objective: profile the multilingual repertoire and dominance configuration
workflow.do_first_because: every multilingual analysis depends on a profiled repertoire

workflow.objective: analyze code-switching, contact outcomes, diglossia, and maintenance/shift
workflow.do_first_because: CS/borrowing and domain confusions are the main multilingual failure modes

workflow.objective: identify speech acts, derive implicatures, and resolve deixis/reference
workflow.do_first_because: force and reference must be fixed before higher pragmatic and politeness inference
universalist models must be culture-checked before use

workflow.objective: analyze cohesion/coherence, conversation structure, and indexical identity work
workflow.do_first_because: interactional analysis needs fine transcripts and participant orientation

workflow.objective: appraise the authority, method, and recency of all candidate sources
acceptance_tests: each source has a method+recency appraisal
workflow.do_first_because: weak sources must be filtered before synthesis to prevent rework

workflow.objective: integrate appraised findings and judge transfer to the target community
acceptance_tests: every claim states community of origin and transfer limit
exit_criteria: answer synthesized with transfer caveats and review passed
workflow.do_first_because: transfer over-generalization is the highest-risk failure and must be gated and reviewed

priority_rationale.notes: root: fixes population and frame for all retrieval
makes constructs measurable before any analysis
high-risk gate: filters weak sources before synthesis
highest-risk output node; gated and human-reviewed
high-coupling inference layer over speech acts
depends on variable analysis; screens age-grading
reference resolution supporting acts and CA
regional layer; lower coupling, sequenced last

dominance_rules.trigger: a fast answer would skip transfer/appraisal gates
dominance_rules.required_action: complete appraisal and transfer gates before answering
dominance_rules.example: shipping a synthesis before source appraisal

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is unblocked but its prerequisite is unmet
dominance_rules.example: doing CS analysis before profiling the repertoire

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number is offered without an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: label as heuristic unless a source supports more
dominance_rules.example: claiming an 'observed' factor weight with no dataset

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is about to lock with failing checks
dominance_rules.required_action: resolve failing checks before any lock
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking a synthesis with an unresolved contradiction

dominance_rules.trigger: a risk>=0.80 or transfer decision is being automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk or irreversible decisions

dominance_rules.trigger: adding content would break the schema contract
dominance_rules.required_action: preserve the contract; trim content instead
dominance_rules.example: adding a node that omits required fields

dominance_rules.trigger: fluent prose would compromise strict JSON
dominance_rules.example: adding commentary outside the JSON object

dominance_rules.trigger: an unsupported claim is asserted with certainty
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade or remove the unsupported claim
dominance_rules.example: stating a universal politeness law with no cross-cultural evidence

dominance_rules.trigger: a universal pragmatic model contradicts culture-specific evidence
dominance_rules.rule: culture-specific evidence caps universal pragmatic models
dominance_rules.example: applying B&L universals against South Asian indirectness norms

dominance_rules.trigger: a general claim would override community-specific evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: mark transfer as a flagged hypothesis
dominance_rules.example: exporting one community's prestige finding to all

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequence would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker link to sequence/feedback

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is created without traceable grounding
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs and a trace or drop it
dominance_rules.example: adding an edge with no source or rationale

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the variety/community before retrieving evidence
anti_rework_rules.rationale: retrieving for the wrong population wastes the whole search
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: sources gathered before scope is set
anti_rework_rules.example: collecting Punjabi sources before deciding which variety

anti_rework_rules.rule: operationalize constructs before sourcing claims about them
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: claims sourced for a vague construct

anti_rework_rules.rule: profile the repertoire before any multilingual analysis
anti_rework_rules.rationale: CS/diglossia/contact claims need the repertoire fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: assigning a matrix language with no dominance data

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the speech act before deriving implicature/politeness
anti_rework_rules.rationale: inference built on a misread act cascades
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: implicature derived before the act is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: reading an indirect refusal as agreement then deriving implicature

anti_rework_rules.rule: appraise sources before synthesizing an answer
anti_rework_rules.rationale: synthesizing weak sources forces full re-do
anti_rework_rules.example: averaging an outdated and a current study without appraisal

anti_rework_rules.rule: decompose inter- vs intra-speaker variation before interpreting
anti_rework_rules.rationale: double-counting variation corrupts every later claim
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: one token credited to both class and style
anti_rework_rules.example: reading a class marker also as a pure style marker

anti_rework_rules.rule: decide CS vs borrowing before counting it as either
anti_rework_rules.rationale: miscoding propagates into contact and change claims
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an item counted as both switch and loan
anti_rework_rules.example: calling an integrated loan a code-switch

anti_rework_rules.rule: model conflict axes before writing dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules with no conflict map are ungrounded
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a resolution rule for an unmodeled tension

anti_rework_rules.rule: write acceptance tests before locking high-risk nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking an untested high-risk node hides defects
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a risk>=0.80 node locked with no tests
anti_rework_rules.example: locking the synthesis with no transfer test

anti_rework_rules.rule: attach transfer caveats before finalizing the answer
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an uncaveated answer over-generalizes and needs full rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: answer finalized with no transfer limits
anti_rework_rules.example: stating a finding as universal with no community-of-origin note
